name: Rausudake from Iwaobetsu (羅臼岳)
why: The highest peak of the Shiretoko peninsula: old forest, a snow gully, alpine flowers on Rausudaira and from the rocky top the Sea of Okhotsk and Kunashiri Island.
book: No permit, but you must sign the climbers' register at Kinoshita-goya hut by the trailhead, where the staff also post bear news. 15 free parking spaces at Iwaobetsu Onsen, 30 minutes by car from Utoro; a few buses a day reach Iwaobetsu. The trail is closed at once when a bear causes trouble: check Shari town news before you go.
water: No huts and no toilets on the mountain (bring a portable toilet: there is a booth). Do not drink the streams (echinococcus): carry 2-3 litres.
dangers: Brown bears: a hiker was killed on this trail in August 2025 and it was closed again in July 2026 after a bear chased a walker. Do not go alone, make noise, carry bear spray.
Snow lies in the Osawa gully into July: slippery and steep, light crampons help early in the season.
Fog, wind and cold on the open ridge and the summit boulders, even in August.
Over 1,400 m of climb on rough rock: a long day.
turnaround: Not at Rausudaira by 11:00, or the summit in cloud: turn back there; the descent takes 3-4 hours.

points.name: Iwaobetsu Onsen trailhead
points.note: About 230 m, behind Hotel Chinohate. Sign the register at Kinoshita-goya; the path climbs at once into dense forest.

points.name: Rausudaira
points.note: A saddle of stone pine and alpine flowers at about 1,400 m, after the Osawa snow gully, about 4 hours up past the Ginreisui spring.

points.name: Rausudake summit
points.note: 1,661 m, a pile of volcanic boulders an hour above Rausudaira: the Okhotsk Sea on one side, Kunashiri on the other. Return the same way.
